name: Victoria
note: In Victoria the doctor notifies the Registrar of the death and its cause within 48 hours, and the funeral director (not the family) gives the registration particulars within 7 days after burial or cremation; reportable deaths go to the coroner, whose court tells the Registrar. Cremation cannot be authorised without the doctor's notice or a coroner's release. From the register, death lists go to the AEC by Commonwealth law; other onward routes are the national arrangements in the Commonwealth layer.

steps.title: Reportable death reported to the coroner or police
steps.who: Any person with reasonable grounds to believe a reportable death has not been reported (police and doctors in practice).
steps.trigger: A death that is unexpected, unnatural or violent, follows a medical procedure unexpectedly, occurs in custody or care, is of an unknown person, or for which no doctor's notice under BDMR Act s 37 will be signed.
steps.summary: Reportable deaths go to a coroner, the Victorian Institute of Forensic Medicine or a police station; failing to report is an offence (20 penalty units). The doctor must then not issue the s 37 notice.

steps.title: Doctor notifies the Registrar of the death and its cause
steps.who: The doctor responsible for the person's medical care immediately before death, or a doctor who examines the body after death.
steps.summary: The doctor sends the cause-of-death notice straight to the Registrar in the form and manner the Registrar approves; failure is an offence (12 penalty units).

steps.title: Doctor gives notice of the death to the funeral director

deadline.text: when the s 37(1) notice is given

steps.summary: The doctor also notifies the funeral director or other person arranging disposal; that notice is one of the documents that allows cremation.

steps.title: Coroners Court tells the Registrar of a coronial death and its outcome
steps.who: The principal registrar of the Coroners Court.
steps.trigger: A coroner is notified of a death; later the body is released or a finding made.

deadline.text: as soon as practicable after receiving the notification

steps.summary: The Coroners Court informs the Registrar when a death is reported and sends the release, determination or finding of cause later.

steps.title: Cremation authorisation requires the doctor's notice or a coroner's release
steps.who: The applicant (usually the funeral director) applies to the cemetery trust running the crematorium.
steps.summary: Cremating without a cremation authorisation is an offence. The application must include a medical practitioner's certificate and the doctor's s 37(2) notice, or a coroner's release order.

steps.title: Funeral director notifies the Registrar after disposal
steps.who: The funeral director or other person who arranges disposal of the remains.
steps.trigger: Burial or cremation of the remains.

deadline.text: within 7 days after disposal of the remains

steps.summary: The person arranging disposal, not the family, carries the duty to give the Registrar the death registration particulars, with supporting documents; failure is an offence (5 penalty units). If remains are not disposed of within 30 days of death, the custodian must notify instead.

steps.title: Registrar registers the death
steps.who: The Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages (Victoria).
steps.trigger: Receipt of the doctor's or coroner's notice and the funeral director's notice.
steps.summary: The Registrar registers the death by making an entry in the Register, and may register on incomplete particulars; a coronial death can be registered before the inquiry ends.

steps.title: Death certificate issued on application with an adequate reason
steps.who: Any applicant who states their interest and shows an adequate reason, judged by relationship, age and contents of the entry.
steps.summary: Certificates are issued after a search of the Register and are evidence in legal proceedings. Before a coronial inquiry ends the certificate is endorsed as an incomplete registration.

steps.title: Registrar notifies the Voluntary Assisted Dying Review Board
steps.who: The Registrar, to the Voluntary Assisted Dying Review Board.
steps.trigger: Registration of a voluntary assisted dying death.
steps.latencyNote: must notify the Review Board; no time set (s 40A read) (bdm-s40a)
steps.summary: Where a death followed voluntary assisted dying, the Registrar must notify the Review Board of the registration.

steps.title: Registrar sends monthly death lists to the AEC
steps.who: The Victorian Registrar as Registrar-General for the Commonwealth Electoral Act.
steps.trigger: Registration of a death of a person aged 16 or over.

deadline.text: after the beginning of each month

steps.summary: Commonwealth law; see the au-commonwealth layer.

steps.title: Organisations may be given access to Register information on conditions
steps.who: Any person or organisation the Registrar is satisfied has an adequate reason, on conditions set by the Registrar.
steps.summary: Section 48 is the Victorian legal basis for giving organisations access to, or extracts from, the Register; the national Australian Death Check and data feeds sit in the au-commonwealth layer.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: No deadline from death: the doctor must notify within 48 hours of death, and the funeral director within 7 days after disposal of the remains (or a notice if not disposed of within 30 days).

informantDuty.note: The funeral director or other person arranging disposal must notify the Registrar; the doctor separately notifies the death and cause.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent medical examiner review; the attending or examining doctor notifies the Registrar directly, and reportable deaths go to the coroner.

electronicRegistration.note: Notices are 'in a form and manner' approved by the Registrar; the Act does not specify electronic lodgement and the BDM Victoria site was unreachable.

certificateAccess.note: The applicant must state their interest and show an adequate reason; the Registrar weighs relationship, age and contents of the entry.

gaps: Who may verify (pronounce) death: no Victorian statute found; nurse/paramedic verification rests on health-service policy not read.
www.bdm.vic.gov.au and www.vic.gov.au were blocked by egress policy, so the online death-registration channel for funeral directors and certificate eligibility rules in practice were not read.
Statistics (ABS/AIHW) supply from the Victorian registry not found in the Act; NSW's equivalent is documented, Victoria's was not.
